1-2: Whole hours: when a cartoon or a walk starts or ends.
Half hours and quarter hours added to a time.
How long something lasts, from its start and its end.
Sleep across midnight: from a time in the evening to a time in the morning.
A bus trip in minutes, from leaving to arriving.
A clock that strikes the hours: how many strokes in a few hours.
A time some minutes before or after a given time, crossing the hour.
Two activities one after another, with a break between them.
Which of two films is longer, from their start and end times.
A timer for cooking: when to start so that the food is ready at a given time.
3-4: A lesson or a trip across the hour, in hours and minutes.
Minutes in a few hours and a half.
Sleep from a time at night to a time in the morning, on the 24-hour clock.
A clock that strikes the hours and once at every half hour: the strokes in a day.
A watch that loses or gains minutes every hour: what it shows later.
A bus leaving every few minutes: when the bus of a given number leaves.
A time a while ago: hours and minutes taken away, crossing the hour.
A school day of lessons with breaks between them: when it ends.
The 24-hour clock and the 12-hour clock: the same moment written both ways.
Two clocks set at the same time, one fast and one slow: the difference after some hours.
5-6: A night shift with breaks: how long it lasts across midnight.
Phoning between time zones: the time at the other end.
A flight across time zones: the local times of take-off and landing.
Two night trains: which trip is longer, and by how much.
Two buses on one route, one every 12 minutes and one every 18: when they next leave together.
A film shown twice with a break between: when the second showing ends.
A flight there and back: the time in the air and the difference between the zones.
A watch that gains a few minutes each hour: the true time when it shows a given time.
Two clocks, one gaining and one losing: when they show the same time again.
The angle between the hands of a clock at a given time.
